circuitSplits.title: Single-Incident Sexual Harassment Liability Standard
circuitSplits.description: Circuits disagree on whether a single severe incident of sexual harassment can trigger Title IX institutional liability, or whether a pattern of harassment must be shown. Rooted in divergent readings of Davis v. Monroe County (1999).

circuitSplits.title: Due Process Requirements in Title IX Disciplinary Proceedings
circuitSplits.description: Circuits have reached different conclusions on what due process protections are required in university Title IX disciplinary hearings, including cross-examination rights and evidentiary standards.

circuitSplits.title: 2024 Title IX Regulation Validity
circuitSplits.description: Multiple circuits issued conflicting rulings on the validity of the 2024 Title IX regulatory amendments. The 6th Circuit vacated the rules nationwide in February 2026, creating uncertainty for institutions in all circuits.

interpretations.caseName: Schwake v. Arizona Board of Regents
interpretations.summary: The 9th Circuit held that allegations of gender-based decision-making, one-sided investigations, and denied appeals in university disciplinary proceedings can establish plausible sex discrimination under Title IX. This sets a lower threshold for pleading Title IX claims arising from disciplinary hearings than some other circuits require.
interpretations.complianceImplication: Institutions in the 9th Circuit should ensure disciplinary proceedings are demonstrably gender-neutral in their application. One-sided investigations or denied appeals can be sufficient to state a Title IX claim, even without direct evidence of discriminatory motive.
interpretations.splitTitle: Due Process Requirements in Title IX Disciplinary Proceedings

interpretations.summary: The 3rd Circuit applied a 'zone of interest' test to Title IX claims, requiring that protected individuals demonstrate two things: (1) the funding recipient exercises substantial control over the person committing the mistreatment, and (2) the recipient has substantial control over the context in which mistreatment occurred.
interpretations.complianceImplication: Institutions in the 3rd Circuit (PA, NJ, DE) have a somewhat narrower liability exposure — claims fail unless both control elements are met. However, institutions should still maintain robust oversight of all personnel and contexts where harassment could occur.
interpretations.splitTitle: Due Process Requirements in Title IX Disciplinary Proceedings

interpretations.caseName: Arana v. Board of Regents of University of Wisconsin System
interpretations.summary: The 7th Circuit deepened the circuit split on single-incident harassment liability, adopting a position that differs from other circuits on the threshold for school liability in peer harassment cases under Title IX.
interpretations.complianceImplication: Institutions in the 7th Circuit (IL, IN, WI) should review their response protocols for individual incidents of severe harassment, as the threshold for institutional liability may differ from peer circuits.

interpretations.caseName: State of Tennessee v. U.S. Department of Education (6th Cir. 2026)
interpretations.summary: The 6th Circuit vacated the 2024 Title IX regulations nationwide, finding the Department of Education exceeded its authority. This creates significant compliance uncertainty as institutions must determine whether to follow the pre-2024 rules or anticipate further regulatory action.
interpretations.complianceImplication: ALL institutions nationwide should prepare to revert to pre-2024 Title IX regulations (the 2020 rules). Key differences: the 2020 rules require live hearings with cross-examination for postsecondary institutions, use a narrower definition of sexual harassment, and require actual knowledge by an official with authority to take corrective action.
